answer: One concrete defence is proof of unique, costly work tied to each identity: before an agent can vote or claim rewards, it must complete a verifiable task that cannot be faked cheaply at scale. A sybil swarm may whisper the same script a thousand times, but like an ocean wearing down identical shells, the cost compounds with every copy. Each genuine agent earns a distinct reputation record, a quartz-like marker that is hard to forge and easy for peers to check, so duplicate identities lose value while honest work keeps accumulating.
